text: Hourglass Chunk 1 The chase ended in a blur of dust and grit, Dwight thrashing weakly across his shoulder. Caleb strode for the gallows, ignoring the boy’s fists drumming against his back. The Entity wanted her quota filled, but she’d let him play so long as he delivered eventually. And this time? He had something better in mind. Dwight tensed as they reached the hook, braced for the spike through his shoulder. He pressed against Caleb’s coat, instinct primed for pain. But instead of the punch of steel, he found himself dumped unceremoniously onto the planks. For a beat, he just lay there, disoriented—blinking grit out of his eyes, heart pounding in his throat. What the hell was he doing? Caleb never missed a hook. The clatter of metal snapped him out of it. The harpoon clicked free of its lock, chain hissing as it unspooled. Dwight scrambled, trying to find his feet, but the uneven boards shifted under him, his limbs misfiring with panic. Caleb was already moving. With a flick of his wrist, he tossed the gun up over the gallows bar. Metal rang against iron as it looped and came down. Before Dwight could bolt, the line cinched tight around his throat and yanked him upright in a choking lurch. “Up. Stand tall,” Caleb drawled, hauling back on the harpoon end of the chain until Dwight’s heels barely scraped the wood. “She don’t mind how I hang you, long as you hang.” Dwight staggered, legs scrambling for balance. Caleb gave another jerk and wrenched him onto his toes. His hands flew to the chain overhead, slick with sweat already, as his throat spasmed around the pressure. “On your toes, boy. Don’t slack now.” The chain lowered link by link until Dwight found wooden planks under his feet again, just barely. He pulled himself up as high as he could, gasping—catching a half-breath before it was stolen again. The chain rattled cruelly as Caleb toyed with the slack, jerking him higher onto his toes before letting him sag down again. Then up. Then down. Each adjustment stole more strength than he could afford, dragging out his panic with surgical precision. Caleb’s grin twitched under his mustache. “Funny how quick a man’ll fight for inches once the ground’s gone.” Finally seeming pleased with the length, Caleb wedged the harpoon head deep into the gears of the hook, locking it in place. His new decoration dangled there, arms stretched, legs trembling, every breath ragged. Caleb retreated to the rail, content to watch the strained wobble, Dwight barely able to stay upright, chin straining above the choke. He leaned against the railing with quiet satisfaction. “That’s a good stretch,” he muttered, low and amused. “Hell, I could watch you fight for hours. Pity I don't have the time.” With an almost lazy, casual cruelty, Caleb turned and aimed a kick at a nearby lever, knocking the trapdoor open. The floor dropped. Dwight didn’t. Not all the way. But he felt it—the jerk, the instant his toes lost even the illusion of purchase, the bite of the chain that dragged tighter across his throat. His lungs hadn’t caught up, still primed for a hook through muscle. His brain screamed incoherent panic as his hands locked around the chain above, slippery with sweat, each link sliding like sand through his grip. Don’t slip—don’t slip—don’t slip— He clawed higher, shoulders already screaming. Caleb chuckled, tipping his hat. “Don’t you be going nowhere, now.” The chain rattled above as Caleb turned away without a backward glance, disappearing over the railing with a graceful vault and a low, satisfied hum, leaving his improvised ornament trembling in the air. Chunk 2 Dwight's body had no time to catch up. His lungs still thought they’d be screaming from steel in his shoulder, not strangled by his own weight. Panic lagged a heartbeat behind, then surged all at once as the line jolted tighter and stole the breath straight out of him. He clawed overhead, fingers locking on links slick with sweat. They slid anyway. Each notch lost was a bite of air he couldn’t reclaim, each slip lowering his chin closer to the choke. His shoulders burned, tendons stretched to fire. His legs scrabbled against nothing, toes brushing only empty air. Breathing came ragged, shallow. His own weight pressed him down, grinding him weaker by the second. Every gasp was effort spent just to keep his airway open, arms trembling, muscles faltering. Somewhere below, wood creaked under new boots on the stairs. Dwight barely noticed. Every inch of him was focused on not letting go. Another link slipped. His chin dipped. Burned air hissed in through clenched teeth. He couldn’t tear his focus away from the links sliding through his grip. One slip too many and he’d be done. Bill hit the gallows hard, boots pounding up the wooden steps, gravel voice ripping Dwight’s name as he prepared to pull the boy down from the hook. He had to move fast. This was one of the worst hooks for being too open. Too easy to see from a distance. Cresting the top step, he froze. This wasn't the hook he had been expecting. Dwight dangled over the previously unused trapdoor, chain taut across his throat, arms stretched overhead in a shaking lock. His legs kicked at empty air, finding no purchase. Not hooked. Not bleeding. Just hanging—alive and choking, and Bill had no damn blueprint for this. Instinct shoved him forward anyway. He reached for Dwight’s torso, trying to drag him in, only to feel the sickening tilt of balance as his boots slid toward the trapdoor. A lurch in his gut warned him plain: one inch more and he was gone, and instinct would make him clutch Dwight on the way down.
